pagerduty-bot: [P1] HIGH error rate detected for /v1/generate in euc1 during 1768554300-1768554320. 5xx spike (500/502) above threshold. Pager: maya a (oncall)

maya a (oncall): seeing the alert. pulling up grafana and envoy stats now. anyone hit by customer pings? :eyes:

sam p: just got a support DM — a single customer reported timeouts ~2m ago. not sure widespread yet.

jihoon k: I'm on network stack. starting with ALB target group healthchecks and NLB metrics for euc1. grabbing ELB logs.

olivia c: I'm on CS side, collecting affected orgs. so far looks like a handful of customers in eu-west but could be broad.

maya a (oncall): traceroute from lambda -> alb shows increased latency to ingress NLB IPs. also Envoy downstream connection resets on Service A pods. stack: ALB -> NLB -> envoy sidecars -> app.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: deploy 2026.02.11-3f4a succeeded to cluster-euc1 at 1768554200 (no automatic rollout).

sam p: could the recent deploy have changed idle timeout or healthcheck headers?

jihoon k: checking target group healthcheck config: looks like a change 1768554140 changed path from /hc to /healthz and timeout from 2s -> 1s. That seems risky with heavier tail latencies.

maya a (oncall): ok that matches timeframe. hypothesis: healthcheck timeout reduction caused targets to flap and ALB started draining. That would cause 502s/backends timed out.

olivia c: customer-visible symptoms: connection resets, some 502s, sticky sessions rebalancing. ramped up around 2:06pm UTC.

jihoon k: quick mitigation: revert healthcheck timeout to 2s and path to /hc for euc1 target groups. executing now.

jihoon k: ```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/euc1-ingress --health-check-path /hc --health-check-timeout-seconds 2
```

maya a (oncall): rolling that change. monitoring target healthy count...

(30s later)

jihoon k: targets starting to mark healthy again, healthy_count returning to expected. connection resets dropping.

sam p: backend 5xx rate decreasing on graphs. still some lingering 502s but looks like recovery.

olivia c: I posted update to affected customers: "We've identified a recent healthcheck config change causing target flapping; we've reverted and are monitoring. Expect degraded traffic to normalize in minutes." responses: thank you, some still seeing intermittent timeouts.

maya a (oncall): good. we should also check ALB deregistration timeout and connection draining settings in case sessions got externally torn. jihoon, can you confirm connection_draining (deregistration delay) was default 300s?

jihoon k: looks like target deregistration delay is 300s. that means some sessions could still be in flight and experience errors while targets come back up.

maya a (oncall): mitigation step 2: increase ALB connection timeout to 60s? wait — altering deregistration delay during incident risky. instead, we're enabling an ingress fallback: route a small % of traffic to overflow NLB in eu-west that uses older config. I'll open a traffic-shift canary via routing policy.

maya a (oncall): ```
redwoodctl traffic-shift --from ingress-euc1 --to ingress-eu-west-fallback --percent 10 --duration 10m
```

infra-bot: routing-change: traffic-shift job started (id=ts-1768554321-1). 10% shift to ingress-eu-west-fallback.

sam p: switch in place. latency improved for some sessions. 502s dropping further.

olivia c: updating CS with new note: "We've shifted 10% of traffic to a fallback ingress to reduce customer errors while targets stabilize." customers replied :thumbsup: and one provided a repro — app regained connectivity after 30s.

maya a (oncall): ok we have recovery trend across the board, cpu and kube pod restarts look normal. marking incident as mitigated but still monitoring for regressions.

(15m later)

jihoon k: postmortem notes so far: root cause = recent healthcheck tweak (path + lowered timeout) rolled to euc1; caused frequent healthcheck timeouts under transient latency -> ALB considered targets unhealthy and started draining -> connection resets and 502s surfaced. Contributing factor: long target deregistration delay (300s) increased user-visible errors during reconvergence.

maya a (oncall): action items: 1) revert healthcheck change in deploy pipeline to require canary in a single region and automated rollback on health degradation; 2) add an automated preflight that validates healthcheck changes against p95 latency for region; 3) reduce deregistration delay for ingress target groups to 60s pending SLA review; 4) improve runbook steps for traffic-shift fallback.

olivia c: I'll prepare customer-facing timeline and runbook blurb for status page.

sam p: I'll open a PR to the infra repo to add deploy guardrails for healthcheck param changes with a 1h review by networking team.

maya a (oncall): handing off to night oncall jihoon k. summary: incident caused by healthcheck timeout/path change in euc1, reverted, enabled 10% traffic shift to fallback, recovering. monitor for 2 hours. any new alerts -> page.

jihoon k: acknowledged. will monitor. I'll attach ALB healthcheck diffs and ELB logs to the postmortem draft.

pagerduty-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1768558120. Severity lowered to P3 pending postmortem.
